class: Two-step account sign-in blocked by visible-email credential guard
symptom: Panasonic Automotive application 569 reached the iCIMS/Auth0 password step after CAPTCHA. The saved password form had a filled password and a read-only, hidden username, but no visible error or transition. The run waited for the owner, saying sign-in did not get past the form. No new failed sign-in was recorded.
site: Panasonic Automotive Network Engineering Lead, login.icims.com, 26 October 2026
root_cause: The credential gateway required one visible filled email control. Auth0 puts the already accepted username in a hidden read-only text control on its password step, so the gateway refused the Log In click. PageAgent marked sign-in as tried before knowing whether that click happened and misclassified the guard refusal as an attempted sign-in.
why_tests_missed: Credential gateway regressions covered combined email/password forms and account creation, but not a two-step password form with the accepted username carried read-only.
fix: Allow the narrowly scoped sign-in gateway to recognize a filled, read-only, hidden username control with username autocomplete on a password-only form. Clear the sign-in-attempt marker and report no attempt when the guard did not dispatch the click. No safety.py change.
prevention: Record whether a guarded credential click actually occurred before treating a password page as a rejected sign-in. Preserve the one-form, one-password, accepted-username and exact Log In label checks.
